Handel: Harp Concerto
Mr Handel has written a concerto for me.
The harp of Wales, for your orchestra.
A harpist from Wales. Handel put a harp concerto for him to play into Alexander's Feast (1736).
His own oboe concertos
My wife's singing and my oboe: the two of us make one concert.
The virtuosity of the oboe, for your orchestra.
A celebrated oboist of the Mannheim (later Munich) court. He toured all Europe with his wife, the singer Franziska, winning ovations with his own concertos.
Festive music for trumpets and timpani
The timpani ride at the head of a prince's procession, sir.
The drums of ceremony, for your orchestra.
A master of trumpet and timpani. In 1795 he wrote a book on their playing, setting down the skills and pride of the court musicians.
Fantasias for oboe
Playing oboes and making them — both are my trade.
The oboe of the Paris Opéra, for your orchestra.
Principal oboe of the Paris Opéra. He made oboes himself, and raised French oboe playing through his improvements to the instrument and his method.
Oboe of the Société des Concerts du Conservatoire
The oboe's sound is the nearest thing to human lament.
The tone of the Paris Conservatoire, for your orchestra.
Professor of oboe at the Paris Conservatoire and founder of the French oboe school. Berlioz prized his tone very highly.
The timpani in Beethoven's Fifth Symphony
I have been building timpani that can change their pitch, you see.
The drums of the Gewandhaus, for your orchestra.
Timpanist of the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra, who played in Mendelssohn's orchestra. He devised machine timpani whose pitch can be changed quickly.
Études for oboe
I took a first prize at the Conservatoire at 15. Now I am learning my trade in the orchestra.
A young oboe, for your orchestra.
An oboist who left the Paris Conservatoire with a first prize at 15. He later became professor there and established modern French oboe playing.

The harp is an instrument for painting water and light.
The harp of Paris, for your orchestra.
A Belgian-born harpist. As professor at the Paris Conservatoire he trained many virtuosos; Renié and Tournier were among his pupils.

The French oboe, for your orchestra.
The great professor of oboe at the Paris Conservatoire. His pupils scattered to the world's orchestras and spread the 'French oboe'.
